chunks: 9. And he said: Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) said:

Do you not see that those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sent for wretchedness against the people of misguidance from the hosts of the satans and their kind are more than what you see sent to the Khalifah of Allah, whom He sent for justice and correctness, from among the angels? It was said: O Abu Ja‘far, how can anything be more than the angels? He said: As Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has willed. The questioner said: O Abu Ja‘far, if I were to narrate this hadith to some of the Shi‘ah, they would reject it. He said: How would they reject it? He said: They would say that the angels (عليهم السلام) are more than the satans. He said: You have spoken truly; understand from me what I say.

There is no day or night except that all the jinn and satans visit the Imams of misguidance, and an equal number of angels visit the Imam of guidance. Then when Laylat al-Qadr comes, there descends in it to the Wali al-Amr, from the angels, and Allah has created — or he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has assigned — from the satans their equal in number. Then they visit the wali of misguidance and bring him falsehood and lies, until perhaps he reaches morning and says: I saw such-and-such and such-and-such. If he were then to ask the Wali al-Amr about that, he would say: You saw a satan that informed you of such-and-such and such-and-such, until he explains it to him with an explanation and makes him know the misguidance upon which he stands.

By Allah, whoever affirms Laylat al-Qadr surely knows that it belongs exclusively to us, because of the statement of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) to ‘Ali (عليه السلام) when his death approached: This is your wali after me; if you obey him, you will be rightly guided. But whoever does not believe in what is in Laylat al-Qadr is a denier, and whoever believes in Laylat al-Qadr from among those who are upon other than our view, truthfulness leaves him no room except to say that it is for us; and whoever does not say so is a liar.

Surely Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is too great to send down the command with the Spirit and the angels to a disbelieving transgressor. If one says that He sends it down to the khalifah whom they follow, then their statement is nothing. If they say that He does not send it down to anyone, then it cannot be that something is sent down to no thing. And if they say — and they will say — this is nothing, then they have gone far astray.

key_terms.أَئِمَّةَ ٱلضَّلَالَةِ: The leaders of misguidance who are visited by jinn and satans.
key_terms.إِمَامَ ٱلْهُدَى: The Imam of guidance who is visited by angels.
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ: The Night of Decree, presented here as a continuing reality linked to divine authority.
key_terms.وَلِيِّ ٱلْأَمْرِ: The divinely authorized guardian to whom the angels descend with the command.
key_terms.ٱلرُّوحِ: The Spirit who descends with the angels and the divine command.
key_terms.ٱلصَّوَابِ: Correctness and truth for which the Khalifah of Allah is sent.
key_terms.ٱلْإِفْكِ: Falsehood brought by the satans to the wali of misguidance.

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith connect Laylat al-Qadr to the Imam and divine authority?
ai.summary: This hadith explains Laylat al-Qadr as an ongoing reality tied to the Wali al-Amr and the Imam of guidance, to whom the angels descend with the divine command. It contrasts the angelic visitation of the Imam with the satanic visitation of the leaders of misguidance, and argues that belief in Laylat al-Qadr entails recognition of divinely appointed authority after the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم).
